data.narrative:
Naïfo Technologies is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aymeric Barthes and Gaëtan Sévérac, having raised €54.7M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies, supplemented by one public comparable (ticker: 277810.KQ) and a broader universe of eight private peers including Hadrian, Nimble Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

The peer-median method, the primary applicable triangulation approach, anchors the analysis to five contemporaneous robotics companies spanning Series B through Series D. The median valuation across this set stands at $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. Sample peers include Exotec at $2.0B (Series D), Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), Dexterity at $1.6B (Series B), Hadrian at $1.6B (Series C), and Nimble Robotics at $1.0B (Series C). This peer distribution reflects heterogeneous stage progression and capital efficiency within the sector.

The triangulated valuation range derived from this methodology is $1.4B (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median estimate of $1.6B. Key uncertainties include the limited sample size (five peers), stage dispersion within the comp set, and nascent public market liquidity in the sector. The peer-median result is most defensible for establishing a central case, while the range bounds reflect observed variation among proximate-stage companies in robotics and manufacturing.
